utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone, also the interpreters' booth and the technical booth. If I'm not mentioning, it doesn't mean that I'm not aware of your presence and of your assistance without which we could not proceed. Mr. Ierace, I think you'll do the last part of the examination-in-chief of your witness. Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness, Mr. Hvaal

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, whilst he's being brought in, at the conclusion of the cross-examination and re-examination of this witness, I would be grateful for an opportunity to say a few words as to the calling of witnesses next week, and some other matters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll give you an opportunity for that. Good morning, Mr. Hvaal. You can hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. The examination-in-chief will continue. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ierace: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hvaal.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the period mentioned yesterday, September 1992 through until August of 1994, did you make any observations on the Bosnian Serb side of the confrontation lines of the participation in the armed conflict of what appeared to be paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whereabouts during that period did you make such observations?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In several locations, when crossing in and out through Ilidza, and also around the Lukavica barracks, and in Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You've mentioned three sites. In relation to Lukavica barracks, what actually did you see?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paramilitaries as one would define them, recognised through non-standard uniform and equipment, driving non-military vehicles, behaving in a - how can I say - non-military or unmilitary fashion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of vehicles did you observe them to be driving?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly rather expensive Belgrade- or foreign-plated vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- mostly wearing uniforms, but not necessarily recognisable as anything from the former Yugoslavia in terms of insignia and such things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what was actually at Lukavica? What was Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lukavica is an army barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any discussions on the topic of the role of the paramilitaries with any members of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps or the -- put it this way: The Bosnian Serb army people?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would have come up. I mean, there was a certain amount of animosity between these two and -- yes, I'm sure, yes, it would have come up, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, keep in mind I'm asking you what you actually remember rather than what would have been said.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what, if anything, you were told by members of the Bosnian Serb army about the compatibility of the role of the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember having at least one conversation with a Bosnian Serb army officer. I believe this took place in the airport. I'm not a hundred per cent sure. But it concerned the -- you know, what role paramilitaries would play after the confrontation lines had become as fixed as they were towards the end of 1993 and onwards. I think -- I can't sort of quote correctly, but I'd say that the conclusion of our conversation would be something to the effect that paramilitaries don't have much of a military role to play in a situation like that. They are largely unsuited for this type of operation. And there's also very little motivation for them to take part in this, because there tends to be a certain financial side to paramilitary operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they tend to be into it for the -- whatever they can steal, loot, whatever you want to call it, as these -- as they usually have very little or no backing from other sources. Once confrontation lines are fixed, you're no longer able to capture property and then -- and to hence loot it. So your role will then be that of a regular military unit, which doesn't, you know, generate income, as it were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that the case, based on your observations, that once the confrontation lines were fixed, there was not much of a role for them to play?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, and the number of visible paramilitary soldiers, you know, decreased significantly towards, oh, the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think earlier you said towards the end of 1993. Which was it, the end of 1993 or the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. If I said 1993, that's wrong. 1992. After the -- the last major involvement of paramilitaries that I can recall witnessing was one of the battles for one of the airport settlements or the part of Dobrinja late in the summer, I think, of 1992, or in the summer of 1992. And after that, when those confrontation lines were more or less fixed, they were more -- you know, the paramilitary aspect slowly dwindled away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given your reference to late summer, I therefore take it that by September, if I remember my seasons correctly in the northern hemisphere, there was no role?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure there was a role. There --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Put it another way --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, I'm not able to give you exact details of Bosnian Serb military operations, but you could still see them. They were, you know, harder to come by. But they would be more than happy to set up their own checkpoints, you know, on the roads in and out of Sarajevo and help themselves to whatever we had in our cars, if indeed not to our cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Themselves [Real-time transcript read "yourselves"].

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that continued for most of the -- but that seemed to be the sort of thing they were more engaged in, and less in actual combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hvaal. Mr. President, that completes the examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Just for the sake of the record, I see that at 9:10:36, it says "to whatever we had in our cars." It's my recollection that the witness then said "or our cars." If that is true -- that's what you said, Mr. Hvaal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that just for the sake of the transcript, that it should be added, or at least it's corrected now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise. I was speaking very fast at that point, I think. The question which appears at line 2 of page 5 appears as one word, "yourselves." I think in fact I might have them "themselves," referring to the cars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready for the cross-examination of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hvaal.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1995, you gave a statement to the investigators of this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, on the 14th and 15th of February, 2001, you gave another statement?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As current occupation, in your statement it is stated that you are a photographer, that is, the statement of 1995, whereas in the statement of 2001, your current occupation is described as photojournalist. Would you please tell us whether there's any difference in these two occupations -- between these two occupations?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. The term "photographer" can be used to span a wider - how shall I say? - array of subjects, but they are used, you know -- you know, they're mixed -- in this context you can call yourself or be called a photographer, photojournalist, photo reporter, documentary photographer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that in April 1992 you arrived in Sarajevo. At that time, what was your occupation, officially speaking? Were you a photographer or a photo reporter at that time when you arrived in Sarajevo, or were you a freelance, independent photo reporter, as you said?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, and throughout most of the work that I did in all of the former Yugoslavia, I was a photojournalist on assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you both took pictures and reported about what you had photographed or seen?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the media world, the term "photojournalist" refers to a photographer who covers journalistic matters. It doesn't necessarily mean that you report about what you see. The reporting aspect usually refers -- it usually is when it comes to a reporter. But a photojournalist basically means you are a photographer who works with journalistic subjects.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April 1992 when you arrived in Sarajevo, what was your task? What kind of assignment did you have at that time?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a visit with a reporter to do a general assessment on the situation in the city. It was a part of a larger project on the situation in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your profession, the profession of photo reporter, does that imply autonomous and impartial reporting from the area where you happen to be?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent that it's possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you arrived in Sarajevo, how well did you know the city? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about April 1992 here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I need some information from you at the time you arrived. That is, when you first came to Sarajevo, did you know the city at that time? I can rephrase the question perhaps and ask you whether that was indeed the first time that you arrived in Sarajevo, that you visit Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not the first time I visited Sarajevo. I had gone there on several occasions during -- I was stationed in Belgrade in 1990 and 1991 covering the war in Croatia, Eastern Slavonia, more specifically. And as part of that, we on quite a few occasions travelled to Sarajevo from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April when you arrived in Sarajevo, how familiar were you with the situation in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say about as familiar as any other journalist working for an international media organisation at the time, based in the area obviously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Sarajevo on that occasion, in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only for very few days. The assignment was cut short.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those several days that you spent in Sarajevo in April 1992, were you able to make an assessment of the situation in Sarajevo in terms of how normal life was in that city? Did it function normally, according to you? What was your opinion?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not function normally. There had already been outbreaks of street fighting, and casualties had already become a daily factor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "street fighting," could you tell us who was opposed in that street fighting?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Units from -- well, in the early stages, there were still units in -- and this is only based on what I could actually see -- units wearing -- soldiers wearing JNA uniforms and soldiers wearing various types of improvised uniforms, soldiers wearing no uniforms at all. Armed civilians, a number of different factions. Situation was fairly confused in April 1992. Depends on when -- we were there very early in April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take pictures of such situations, the situations that you were able to observe in the streets of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did very few photographs during that stay because the assignment was basically aborted for security reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent quite some time in Sarajevo on the whole. Would it be possible for you to identify the locations where that street fighting took place in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're still talking about the April 1992?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in a very accurate manner, no. The situation was very confused, and we avoided travelling around as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're unable to identify specific streets and locations where the fighting took place?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April 1992, well, I could --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you cannot remember or if you don't know, just tell us.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the area around Marsal Tito barracks, for instance, would be one of the places. The -- let me see now. Depends on how long you want me to think, but I can probably come up with a few places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who, as far as you were able to observe, were armed and were wearing various uniforms, during the time that you spent in Sarajevo, did you come to know who those individuals were and which formations they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April of 1992, not especially. But later on, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "later on, yes", what it is that you learned about those armed individuals and the uniforms that you had seen in April?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on we learned -- or I learned to identify some of the insignia, and also the sort of general choice of uniforms to wear that the different sides would adhere to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us about JNA uniforms. I should like to know whether there were any specific marks or signs on the basis of which you could identify the uniforms that were worn by the people you saw in April. Could you describe for us a uniform that you saw.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, these are -- would mostly be camouflage uniforms. They would have different insignia on them, some with letters, some with symbols. I don't think I could give you, you know, an exact description of the various insignia. But this is now a long time ago. I would have recognised them at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay in Sarajevo, did you come to learn what the important characteristics of those uniforms and those individuals were? Did they belong to any specific units? When I say "units," I refer to military formations.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we still talking about April here or are we ...?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we are talking about your stay in Sarajevo. I just need some precision, some explanation for the people that you saw were carrying weapons in April in Sarajevo. Did you later, at any point in time, happen to learn something about them, in view of the fact that you spent almost four years in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you learned the fact that there were units belonging to what was still considered to be the Yugoslav army, that there was what was called the Territorial Defence unit, which had their own insignia, I think, at the time. There were also at least two different types of Croatian or Bosnian Croat units involved at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what Croatian or Bosnian Croat units you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were units from what was referred to as the HVO, and at an early stage there was also a unit referred to as HOS, H-O-S, which was not very significant, but it was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Bosnian units -- did Bosnian units also have their insignia, just as these units had?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "a Bosnian unit," what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean units that are Bosnian. You said that there were Croat and Bosnian units, or else I misunderstood you. And perhaps you consider the Bosnian and Croat units to be one and the same under the auspices of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, Ms. Pilipovic, that as far as I can see on my transcript, that the witness said that there were also at least two different types of Croatian or Bosnian Croat units involved at that time. So the witness was talking -- was testifying that there were Bosnian Croat and not Bosnian units. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, during your stay in April, were you able to identify any Bosnian units or to learn of their existence?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what it is that you mean by that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have told us that in April, units of the Territorial Defence took part in the street fighting. Do you know where these units of the Territorial Defence belonged or to whom they belonged and who was in charge of these units?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's a very non-specific question. The Territorial Defence -- members of the Territorial Defence units that you met at the time would say that it was a unit consisting of, you know, representatives of all three ethnic groups defending the city against outside aggression. That would be the normal definition that they would themselves make. When you talk about leadership, are you referring to the leadership of the Territorial Defence in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a hundred per cent sure that he was already in place in April, but it was later Mustafa Hajrulahovic, as far as I remember, who was the commander of the TO in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When my learned colleague from the Prosecution asked you a question, you spoke about paramilitary units that you had met in the period between September 1992 -- after September 1992 in the areas controlled by the VRS. Could you please tell us: What do you mean when you say "paramilitary units"? What is your definition of a paramilitary unit?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The general definition used on paramilitary units, and one which I agree to, is a unit that operates using military equipment, uniforms, military-type tactics and command structures, but are outside or not, you know, entirely linked into the regular military system or -- yes, the regular military system in one side of a conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay in Sarajevo - and when I mean your stay, I'm referring to the period after your arrival in April until 1995 - did you ever meet any members of paramilitary formations on the other side?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other side as opposed to which side?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to Sarajevo, which was controlled by, as you say, Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that I said that Sarajevo was controlled by the territorial defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hvaal, let's try to not lose time. I think the earlier question to you was about paramilitary people in the areas controlled by the VRS which, I understand, is the area surrounding the city. I think the question was about paramilitary groups within the city controlled by whoever at that very moment. But I think that's your intention, Ms. Pilipovic. Would you then please answer the question, and the other side is the "in the town" side.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is yes, I did see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what uniforms they had, if any? Or let me simplify it: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a mixture of various usually camouflage uniforms, sometimes with civilian clothes mixed in, insignia from whatever unit they felt they belonged to. Yeah, but you know, a sort of general -- let me put it this way: The paramilitary units that existed on the -- what we referred to the "Bosnian Government controlled" parts of Sarajevo were not as well equipped and not as uniformly uniformed as their -- as the paramilitary units on the Bosnian Serb side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you identify some of the units that you encountered in the parts of Sarajevo controlled by the Bosnian Army and the paramilitary units that you encountered in Lukavica on the area -- in the area controlled by the Bosnian Serb army? When I say "identify," I'm referring to any names that they may have had, and do you know any such names?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the name that the units used about themselves on the -- on the Bosnian Government side, but I recall at least two different units being led by two individuals in Sarajevo. They were active in -- at least in 1993. They were led by people nicknamed - I don't remember their real names now -- but nicknamed, for instance, there was a character called Caco, and another named Celo I think. Something like that. You have to forgive my pronunciation. On the Bosnian Serb side, one would frequently, especially in the beginning of this period, come across some members of the unit that was led by Zeljko Raznjatovic, also known as Arkan. There was also in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. beginning, but I don't know how long that lasted, a unit on the Bosnian Serb side that referred to themselves as the "White Eagles," but -- and I'm not sure I actually met a live member of that unit. I think I saw some corpses at some point, but I'm not sure I actually met anyone alive from it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that the paramilitary formations in the territory controlled by the Republika Srpska army functioned up until the end of 1992, as far as you know. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. They still had a presence, but they did not seem to be militarily very active.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about the paramilitary formations on the side controlled by the BH army, the formations that you have just identified for us? So, to be more specific, did they also function independently or were they part of the BH army? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's difficult to be 100 percent specific about this. These units would -- how should I say? They would operate more independently than the units within the regular BH army, if you can call it that. Basically, it appeared to us, as outsiders, with the limited knowledge that we had, that these units had more of a choice as to which operations they chose to take part in or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay in Sarajevo, did you know where the command posts of these units were located?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember going passed one a few times and having it pointed out to me. But I couldn't tell you where that was now. At the time, no. We basically tried to stay away from these units as they were -- all paramilitary forces tend to be bad news for journalists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you return to Sarajevo in 1992 after having left Sarajevo, as you have told us, after a very short period of time in April?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at that time have any knowledge of where the front lines were in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the sense that I had it drawn out on a map to me. And at that stage, they were fluctuating a little bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you go to Lukavica where the barracks were under the control of VRS -- or rather, that was in September. Were you alone, or was there a larger group of journalists that visited that area?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we went several times. They would usually be more than one journalist. But I went by myself on a couple of occasions also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say there were several occasions and there were journalists from other medias, can you tell us what other media these journalists came from?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other international news agencies, television stations, newspapers. Basically representatives of media stationed or more or less permanently stationed in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the names of some of these TV stations or newspapers or press agencies that went to visit the territory of the VRS with you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, could you please indicate to the Chamber, in the light of Rule 90(H), what area we're covering at this moment? Is it the subject touched upon by the examination-in-chief, is it credibility, or is it anything else, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in light of the status of Mr. Hvaal as an independent photojournalist and his observations that he presented to us in the course of the examination-in-chief, the Defence would like to check the credibility of this witness, since the witness kept saying, "We were there." And the Defence would like to verify the credibility of this witness by checking who it was that was in the delegation together with him on those occasions when he was not alone. He told us that these were press agencies, news agencies, and now we would like to -- the witness to identify more specifically the journalists who were also with him on his visit to the positions of the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the credibility issue whether he was alone or not while visiting Lukavica barracks. I'm not quite sure about it, but the question whether he was alone or not was, as far as my recollection goes, not raised in the examination-in-chief. It just said he went to Lukavica barracks. And it was during cross-examination that you came up with the question: Were you alone or were you not alone? So credibility should be limited to the credibility of the examination-in-chief. So if you put any additional questions and then say, "I'm testing the credibility of the witness on these additional questions put to him during cross-examination," I don't think that that's a right understanding of what Rule 90(H) says. Would you please keep this in mind while you continue cross-examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. The Defence understands the provision of the Rule 90(H). Let me remind you that in the examination-in-chief, the witness said - I cannot quote the exact page reference - he said, "We were at a briefing in the Lukavica barracks." And my question is, when he says, "We were at a briefing," my question is: Who was at the briefing in the Lukavica barracks? And that was the question that my learned colleague asked right at the beginning of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand that there is some doubt, as the Defence is concerned, about whether he was alone or not. Yes. Okay. If that's your answer, please proceed. Still, the matter of relevance of -- is still there, but please proceed and we'll see what will come.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please tell us: When you were in Lukavica at the briefing, could you please identify which news agencies were represented by their reporters there, if any.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, when I say "we," it means that when we travel in these areas, I personally was never alone. There was always somebody with me. Now, whether this was a Bosnian Serb army officer or fellow colleagues of the media or media that were from the other side, whether they were Bosnian Serb or Yugoslav or media that had come to visit from the other side of the front line. The group could consist of any of these. It was very rare that one -- or basically, you were never all by yourself. That's why I kept saying "we" in this situation. The -- typically the news agencies represented during these trips would be ourselves, Associated Press, somebody from Reuters, somebody from Agence France Presse, somebody from probably CNN or BBC, and SkyNews. Any or all of those, and additional media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you have now named all those agencies, did you ever, during your visits to the lines where the positions of the Republika Srpska army were, were there ever representatives of the other news agencies there?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, yes, there were -- on occasions there would be representatives of other international news agencies there, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those visits when you all went together, did they also film and interview persons that you met during your visit? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent that it was possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that between September 1992 and August 1994 - let me remind you - you said that you visited the positions held by the Republika Srpska army eight to ten times. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As an estimate, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit the VRS positions before September 1992 or was that the first time when you went there?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe I may have gone before that as well. Yes. I'm pretty certain that I went in June or July, July possibly. Yes, because I went -- yes, I left via the Bosnian Serb-held territory. When I left in August, early September, early September -- no. In August. Sorry. Excuse me. When I left in early August, I went out via Bosnian Serb-held territory, and part of that would include a visit to, you know, some of these areas that were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us, at that time in July, which areas did you visit? When I say "areas," I mean areas controlled by the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drove -- let me see now. I would have gone, I believe, to -- I think I went to Lukavica in order to obtain necessary paperwork to continue my journey, and then I went from there -- no, I couldn't tell you exactly. It's too -- no, I can't tell you exactly where the locations I went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that perhaps you did not visit those areas before September 1992? Do you allow that possibility?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did go to these positions?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Bosnian Serb-held territory before September 1992, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before September 1992, could you tell us at which positions did you go to. And what I mean is the positions under the control of the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you exact locations as to the positions around Sarajevo. It would be first to the airport, and then probably to Lukavica from there. I remember following a UN convoy for part of this trip. And then I went -- from there on, I drove the road, after going through the parts of -- you know, going through the Bosnian Serb-held territory around Sarajevo. I then went -- drove through Bosnia to the border with Serbia on my way to Belgrade. So I am definite that I went there because I still have the receipt that was given to me when my car was confiscated by the Bosnian Serb army on the border with Serbia trying to get to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at the time you were not visiting the positions of the Bosnian Serb army, but you were simply taking -- you were travelling. You were travelling through these areas up to the border with Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was doing both at this time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that journey that you took, could you tell us in which position in relation to the road that you took around Sarajevo, to which position did you arrive and what did you see at that position?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not quite sure I understand that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your journey from Lukavica up to Belgrade in July, did you also visit the positions of the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Lukavica, you are -- at that point, you were in a position of the Bosnian Serb army. The front line was very close to there. At this time, there was very extensive fighting going on in the Dobrinja area, for instance, which is very close to Lukavica, as far as I recall. And that would have been one of the areas that one would have to go to anyway. In my line of work, you try to combine travel and work as much as possible. You try to gather information and observe, if necessary -- or if possible, get photographs as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that there were clashes around Dobrinja and that the front lines were very near, can you tell us what was the distance between the front lines and who was opposed in these battles in the areas you were travelling through? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance from Lukavica barracks to the first, at that point, Bosnian territorial defence-held lines would be several hundred metres. Less than a kilometre, depending on how you define the outlines. And yes, it would be the Bosnian Serb army on one side. At that stage, there was still a presence of paramilitaries from -- from -- I'm not entirely sure which unit. But there was a presence of paramilitaries. And then on the other side, yes, there were the Bosnian territorial defence and other units, such as the HVO, for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to estimate which weapons were used in the fighting? What types of weapons were used in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were -- at this stage, I had been on both sides of the conflict on the confrontation lines in that area. On the -- and with the limited knowledge that I was able to get on the Bosnian Serb army side, there were usual small-arms, machine-guns. In addition, there were tanks, armoured personnel carriers, and aircraft guns, both anti-aircraft machine-guns and machine cannons, and mortars and artillery pieces as well as -- no, I think that was about it. On the Bosnian territorial defence-held side, there was, again, small arms, machine-guns. To my recollection, no anti-aircraft weapons. A few mortars. At that stage, certainly no tanks. But yeah, on both sides -- yeah, no. That would be about the description of the weaponry involved. I think I might have seen rocket launchers, but I'm not a hundred percent sure. They were not very common at that stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were telling us about the weapons, as you say, that belonged to the territorial defence of the Bosnians, you said at the time they did not have tanks. What did you mean by that "at that time"? Do you have any information whether they had tanks at any later stage?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about Dobrinja or Sarajevo here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about the fighting in Dobrinja and the weapons that were used by the Bosnian territorial defence, specifically in Sarajevo. Your reply was that at the time, they did not have tanks. And I understand that during the fighting for Dobrinja you did not see a tank. Was there one at a later stage and when?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the Bosnian territorial defence, later the Bosnian Army, at one stage had at least one tank. I don't think I ever saw it moving under its own power. But -- and I never saw it in Dobrinja. But I am not -- you know, I don't know if there was ever a Bosnian Army or Bosnia territorial defence tank in Dobrinja. But at the time I was there, and I was there several times in June, I did not see any armour, any type of armoured vehicles in Dobrinja at that point. Of course, that doesn't mean that there wasn't one, but I did not see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that between September 1992 and August 1994, you also visited the positions of the army of the Bosnian Serbs. Do you recall when it was the first time you went and which positions you visited?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the first time was probably a visit to Mount Trebevic. I can't be a hundred percent sure about this, but probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we say that that was Trebevic, then, could you tell us what you saw at Trebevic at the time?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, front-line positions in the shape of sandbagged positions and trenches, obviously access roads, that sort of thing. Fortified houses, and troops. I think armoured personnel carriers and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take photographs of the APCs?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably not. It was very restrictive what we were actually allowed to photograph during those visits. But I know I have taken photographs of armoured vehicles and, you know, Serbian -- Bosnian Serb army equipment. But very rarely would you be allowed to do that anywhere near the front lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a front line nearby? And if there was, how far was it? At that part of Trebevic, do you know where the front line was?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't give you an exact distance from those very first visits. It's also very often the case that when - and this is on all sides - when military take journalists to -- into combat zones, they don't necessarily take you to the sort of very furthest front line, that you're actually, you know, several lines away from the front. So it is very difficult sometimes to judge whether you are at the actual very first line or if you are one or two lines back from that. In mountainous terrain, obviously like Mount Trebevic, obviously you don't have clearly defined confrontation lines everywhere because they would be impossible to construct. But it was a question of fortified positions on the Bosnian Serb side looking down on fortified positions on the Bosnian government army side, several hundred metres below.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time when you say that you went to Trebevic and when you visited the positions of the Bosnian Serbs, were there troops there in those positions?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uniforms and sort of standard-issue weapons normally, AK-47s, and at that stage I think many were wearing helmets. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe for us if this was a military unit and how many soldiers were in it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appeared to be a military unit, because it was reasonably well organised. They all had similar, if not identical, uniforms and equipment, mostly sort of JNA-style equipment and uniforms. And the officer or officers - I don't remember - accompanying was able to, you know, effectively move around without being hindered in any way by these soldiers. It was obvious that there was a chain in command -- a chain of command in place and that they had been, you know, briefed about the fact that we were coming. And, you know, it wasn't a -- it seemed reasonably well organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, at 11:52, to the question of my colleague whether you had noticed artillery, you answered: "No. We only saw the empty cartridges." Could you tell us, when you said that you did not see artillery, what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't think that that question fairly puts the evidence of the witness yesterday. He said that in some instances he did not see artillery, but that did not apply across the board, so as to speak. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then please quote literally, Ms. Pilipovic, since there's an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it helps to save time, I don't require my learned friend on this occasion to put the exact words, but simply to incorporate into her question that it was only in relation to some of the sites he visited that he did not have his expectation of finding artillery fulfilled. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you, in either way, rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the question of my colleague if you had noticed artillery, could you perhaps tell us in which locations you went to and did not see, did not observe artillery. And when I say "positions," I mean the positions of the Bosnian Serb army that you did not notice artillery.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a question -- this would happen either way. Sometimes we would request and be permitted to go to somewhere because we had reason to believe that there was outgoing artillery fire from that location, for instance, on Mount Trebevic. We would then get there and there would, more often than not, not be an artillery piece in the location that we had requested to go, but very often we would see traces of artillery positions, whether it be -- and I can include tanks in that, because very often you can't really tell the difference whether it's outgoing tank fire or outgoing artillery fire. But more often than not, we would not find an artillery piece in the location that we had asked to go to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the positions of the army of Republika Srpska, the positions in Mount Trebevic, you just explained that you were in certain situations and that there you did not see artillery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In certain situations I would not see artillery, and in other situations I would see artillery, yes. But more often than not, there would not be artillery present in the locations that we had requested to go to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, during examination-in-chief, you answered my colleague's question regarding the locations, the elevations that you were able to identify what could be seen on the other side. So if you were on the demarcation line which is under the control of the army of Republika Srpska, what were you able to see or identify on the other side? I will remind you: You said that in those positions you were able to see buildings, streets, cars. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that was at 11:54:08.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I said that I could -- it would sometimes be possible to identify cars, meaning that we would, for instance, recognise our own vehicles, and you would also be able to see people, obviously. We're talking about distances of a few hundred yards or metres, a few hundred metres in many cases here. So it's obviously possible in daylight to see people, individual people and groups of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just be a little more specific about these elevations that you visited and from which you were able to identify buildings, cars, and, as you say, people?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: From positions such as above the Jewish cemetery, from -- certainly from -- well, that's not an elevated position, but from Lukavica you could see people in Dobrinja, but that again is not elevated. From - let me see now - from the area at and around what we referred to as Sharp Stone feature, where you can look down on the Sedrenik area, and also from tall buildings in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your reply just now, you said that the streets, buildings, and pedestrians or people could be also identified from the Sharp Stone feature. Could you tell us if you ever went to the positions of the Sharp Stone?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go to the position, the one on Sharp Stone, as such, but I went to one - sorry - to the south-east of it, I believe, east/south-east of Sharp Stone feature, to my recollection. I'm not 100 per cent sure, but you could clearly see the Sharp Stone feature position from there. Again, I'm not a hundred per cent sure of the direction from Sharp Stone this position was in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not go to the position of Sharp Stone itself?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to my recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us in which part of Sarajevo were these positions, as you say, the Sharp Stone feature?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where they are? Where is Sharp Stone feature? Is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In which part of the city? How far were you from the Sharp Stone, since you said you did not go to the Sharp Stone? So from Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. which -- how far were you from it and from which position you saw it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the name of the location or indeed if it has a name. Obviously, it would be near to the area called Sedrenik, but on the BSA side of the confrontation line. From, I'd say, several hundred metres away from Sharp Stone feature. But exactly how many hundred metres, I couldn't tell you. Less than a kilometre, definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, in relation to the city of Sarajevo, where Sedrenik is. And if I can perhaps help you. In relation to where your accommodation was. And to remind you, this was near the Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be north-east, as far as I recall. Sedrenik is roughly north-east, north/north-east, perhaps, from the Kosevo -- Sedrenik is north-east or east from Kosevo Hospital, and Sharp Stone is -- Sharp Stone looks down on Sedrenik from the north, roughly, I think. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, from the map that we have, which is the evidence piece of the Prosecution P3644, the Defence copied a part which encompasses a part of the Kosevo Hospital and Sedrenik. With your permission, Your Honour, I made enough copies of this, and I would like to suggest to the witness if he could identify on this map Sedrenik, as well as the Sharp Stone feature, and perhaps explain where he was at the time when he said that he was in Sedrenik. If he can mark it for us on the map. And that would be the Defence evidence piece D29. With your permission, Your Honour, I would like to ask the witness to have a look at the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have it tendered as evidence, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. Of course, the witness has testified, I think several times, that he had some difficulties in finding -- locating the exact spot where he was. So what -- whether this will result in any useful information, we'll have to wait and see, but please keep that in mind when you present the map to the witness. And you also said -- but let me just look. I'm just trying to find the place where he said that he was in Sedrenik. You just asked him to identify the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday, at 12:22:36 -- 12:26, the witness was talking about the Sharp Stone feature, and he also mentioned Sedrenik in his answer to the question of my learned colleague, and he was explaining -- I believe he was telling us about the road that he took up to Sedrenik, and when he was talking about the Sharp Stone in Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to ask Mr. Usher to show a part of the map which is only showing part of the Kosevo Hospital and Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, before we start this exercise of marking, perhaps we could have a break first because the ELMO always takes some time. If this would be a suitable moment for you, then we'll adjourn until 11.00, but not after having heard the observation Mr. Ierace seems to want to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Very briefly, Mr. President, thank you for that. It seems to me from what I can see at this distance, this is a map the Prosecution has not previously seen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand it's part of -- it's indicated by Ms. Pilipovic that it's part of Map P3644. And I can understand if we only need a limited part of it, just a cutout of this map. But during the break, you'll certainly be able to verify whether this is the same black and white big map, or at least part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we'll adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I spoke to my learned friend during the break, and indeed it is a different map. I now have a photocopy of the relevant portion of that map. I have no objection to the use of a map at all. I also indicate for the record that to my right is Darryl Mundis, a member of the Prosecution trial team. He will be taking some witnesses in the scheduled sniping incident phase of the trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Ms. Pilipovic, I'm a bit surprised that you present the map as a part of another map which it turns out not to be. But since there's no objection from the Prosecution side, you may proceed. But as you understand, this Chamber always appreciates precision very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe I was precise enough. I referred to the map specifically, P63644 -- 3644. It's one of the maps that we received from the Prosecution. And the Defence wishes to use one of these maps, and they are all marked for identification as P3644, all of them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps if it was not justified, the words I mentioned, please proceed, and we'll not pay much attention to it. And of course, then apologies as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on this portion of a map which is in front of you, would you please identify the Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kosevo Hospital is in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to ask you to circle the area and mark it with number 1.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which colour would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have to use the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have the black one, I think.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the hospital, would you please identify for us the area of Sedrenik where you said you were present when the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please mark it with number 2.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that you had witnessed an incident in Sedrenik when you came across a group of people who were hiding in a building there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hiding behind a building, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I say "building," I refer to the building that you described was located in Sedrenik. And when you spoke about the group of people who were hiding in that building, I would like to ask you to describe for us that particular building in Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it was a private house or parts of a private house that had been destroyed. But that's as far as I can go. There are several buildings in that area. I couldn't tell you exactly what the building looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please identify for us the location which you said is called the Sharp Stone feature in relation to Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it's in that general area, but I can't give you a one hundred percent precise location. You don't see the elevation very clearly on this map, so it's difficult to see what's high and what's low in the terrain. But it is in the forested area that is above Sedrenik, to my recollection. It's also more or less directly lined up with Visnjik, which is the street I lived on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you mark the location with number 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that there was a flag hoisted on the Sharp Stone feature. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whose flag it was?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would assume it was a Bosnian Serb army flag. It was red, white, and blue striped. You couldn't really tell the details unless you went very close, but -- yes, based on assumption, yes, and the fact that it was known to be a Bosnian Serb army position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the location where you marked as the Sharp Stone feature location, and you said that VRS positions were there, so in relation to that area, do you know and can you tell us where the BH army positions were? You told us they were some 300, 400 metres below the elevation. If you don't know, just say so, please.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that from my recollection, they would be -- obviously, between these two circles that I've drawn here there would be, as far as I remember, a line of confrontation. Now, this area is very hilly. It's very difficult to draw out the precise confrontation line, and I wouldn't remember what it looked like at a later stage anyway. But basically, the BH army controlled most of the built-up part of Sedrenik, where there were houses, buildings, that sort of thing. And so far as I remember, there's a little bit of a hill, and down in the little valleys and area around here, the confrontation line would run, but in a complicated pattern, without sort of clearly defined confrontation lines. But again, this is -- I can't give you a precise indication of where the lines went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Sedrenik, where exactly did the line go, the front line go towards the Kosevo Hospital, since you travelled from the Kosevo Hospital towards Sedrenik? If you don't know, just --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was travelling with a local translator at the time. We were in a hurry. I don't recall the exact route we took. I remember taking a fairly complicated road to get there, and I don't think we travelled along the confrontation line as such. So I wouldn't be able to tell you, based on that, where the confrontation line went. It would obviously be in our best interest to avoid the confrontation line as much as possible in order to get there and back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the hospital, since you lived there for a while, would you be able to tell us where the front line was in relation to the hospital, facing north -- both north and south, and then east and west? Where was it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's a rough assumption, but as far as I recall, the nearest area held by the BSA would be in the higher, sort of more mountainous part of this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the map could be adjusted on the overhead projector so that we can see what he's pointing to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I would say perhaps as close as this. But again, this would, you know, fluctuate during the war and there wouldn't be, you know, an exact description. And then quite far, I mean several kilometres to the north, before -- you would actually -- yes, at least one, maybe more. Because there was a hill due north of the hospital and the area that the hospital was in. I believe there was a children's hospital or something, maternity hospital, sitting on top of that hill, and beyond that the front Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. lines were, and also to the west. We're also talking a distance of several hundred, possibly more, metres. But I'm not -- like I said yesterday, I don't have, unfortunately, a photographic memory, so I wouldn't be able to give you an accurate, you know, drawing of the confrontation lines, you know, at any given time during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know where exactly the front line lay in this part of the town?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew at the time, because you could see them, but to remember now that many kilometres of front line based on drawings on a black-and-white photocopied map is very difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told us that there was an elevation, a hill, above the hospital, do you know the name of that hill, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that the name of the hill is Hum, would that ring a bell? Did you hear about this hill when you were in Sarajevo? Do you know under whose control that hill was?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a radio and television mast on Hum. Are we talking about the same place here? To my recollection, there is a radio and television mast on top of Hum, unless I'm -- there is? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That area was highly contested. I don't think -- I know that the BH army held parts of the mountain, but I can't tell you how far up. There was a Bosnian Serb presence there as well. I remember going there several times and that, you know, it would be a very dangerous area to operate in, but I can't remember exactly how far up it we would be able to go before we would come too close to the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us you had gone to that hill on several occasions. Did you visit the positions of both sides or just the positions of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Hum?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think only of the BH army, as far as Hum is concerned. But I would have been in the area near Hum, but further. I don't think we went onto the actual mountain with the Bosnian Serb army, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were there on several occasions. In view of that fact, could you tell us what kind of view one has of Sarajevo from that hill? What part of the town is visible from Hum? And in particular, what exactly is it that you see in town from that elevation?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you an accurate answer on that. I know you can see the television masts from large parts of the city, so you have a fairly good view. But as to precisely what angles you can see from that location, no, I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately what you can see from that hill? I understand it was a long time ago; however, you spent almost four years in Sarajevo, according to what you testified. Can you perhaps remember what is visible from that hill?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I didn't spend four years on Hum, though, and I went to many other high locations. So it's hard to remember what the view is from the different locations. I mean, obviously from that location, you can see the taller buildings. I can't point out exactly -- I don't want to be imprecise and give you an inexact answer, so I'd rather not say specifically which buildings you can and cannot see from that location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've just told us that while you were in Sarajevo, you went to many other high locations around the town. Could you perhaps tell us, if you know, the names of those hills.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we've mentioned Trebevic already. Then there are -- to the east where the end of the city as it were, there is an elevated area on both sides of the mountain pass that goes out there. I went to Mojmilo Hill on a number of occasions. I went to the -- I can't remember the name of that, but the sort of built-up area that is north. I can't remember the name now. Sort of in the central part of town but to the north slightly. I can't remember the name, sorry. And then many other places, but it's not -- you know, we don't always write down and note the different names of these different locations. And you try to travel with somebody who knows this so that you can spend your time doing your job rather than reading maps and, you know, not getting lost basically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you had gone to Mojmilo hill on a number of occasions. Whose positions were there? Which army controlled the Mojmilo Hill, the VRS or the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question does not make clear the time to which my friend is referring. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained. Could you please specify as far as the time is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was referring to the period between 1992 and 1994. So during that period of time, I should like the witness to tell us when he went to the Mojmilo Hill. And in view of the fact that he had gone there several times, perhaps we can begin by hearing when he went there for the first time and, if he did, whether it was in 1992 or later.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there the first time on June 23 of 1992. I walked in with a Bosnian territorial defence unit that was going to Dobrinja. At that stage, there were still Bosnian Serb units in control of large parts of Mojmilo Hill. The western part of Mojmilo Hill where I believe there is some sort of installation, a reservoir or something like that, I can't remember exactly what it is, but the western part of Mojmilo Hill towards Nedzarici was under control of Bosnian Serb forces at that stage when I walked in the first time. To my recollection, in -- during that summer, I would say later in June or in July, that Serb position on Mojmilo Hill fell to the Bosnian territorial defence, and most of Mojmilo Hill was then under the control of Bosnian Government forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, you testified yesterday that in 1993, you went to the area of Sarajevo where four high-rise buildings are located, four skyscrapers, and you told us that the area in question was Grbavica. Is that correct? Is that the neighbourhood where those four skyscrapers are located?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you had visited the positions of snipers there. Could you tell us what they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms. Basically the same type of uniforms that you came across on most front-line positions on -- you know, in the BSA-held territory. They were similar to the ones that you would see on the checkpoints that we drove through every day. For instance, on the Sierra 4 checkpoint on the road to the airport which we travelled through many times a week, the uniforms and the insignia at that checkpoint was basically very similar to the ones that you would come across elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. How many snipers were there at the time you went there?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't really tell you. How would you define a sniper in this context?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, my question to you was how many snipers were there at the time you visited the location.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only answer that I was in a sniper position, which I can identify from experience, from having seen it many times before. I can tell you that there were uniformed soldiers there, and that there were rifles and machine-guns equipped with sniper scopes. But I cannot tell you whether or not these people were actually snipers. That is impossible to tell from their uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When visiting those positions, did you go to one of those buildings, or did you go to all of them?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I went to two of them. I'm reasonably sure I went to two of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us at what floors were you in those buildings?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fairly high up, but I can't tell you the exact floors. It's too long ago. I would say at least seven, eight floors, something like that. But you know, you're going very quickly up a staircase which doesn't have windows, and it's difficult to count as you go up and down. You're also conscious of the fact that you're very close to the front line, so you're trying to avoid being seen. So counting floors is sort of not your main preoccupation. So I couldn't give you an exact figure on which floor, no. But fairly high up in the building, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that there were no windows on the buildings. Were those buildings inhabited by people?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall saying that there were no windows. That's not correct. These buildings definitely have windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say that they did not have any doors?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe I said that either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Looking at the transcript, I read that the witness has testified that on the staircases, there were no windows, which made it difficult for him to find out at what floor he was. I think that's my recollection I think supported by the transcript. If this would clarify the problem --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. The windows, if there were windows in the staircases, they would have been covered up to avoid detection by people moving up and down. So whether or not there were actually windows in the staircases, I can't remember. But effectively speaking, you can't look out or be seen moving through these staircases, to my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hvaal. You may proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that there were curtains. Could you please clarify. Do you know why the curtains were there?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Curtains?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Ms. Pilipovic -- there might be a translation problem -- is referring to your answer saying that if there were windows in the staircase, they would have been covered up to avoid detection by people moving. That's what you -- so the cover, whether these were curtains or blankets or sheets I don't think is of major importance. But I think that's what the question was about.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay in that building, did you talk -- did you meet any people on the eighth floor or on the highest floor where you were, as you said?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I went to the highest floor, but I went to one of the higher floors. Yes, I did speak to some people in the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on one of the higher floors, as you say, did you see any armed Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in at least one of the locations there was obviously -- are you talking about weapons they were carrying or weapons that were there in the room?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Weapons that they carried.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Weapons that they carried. Probably only sidearms, because there were people who were inside rooms in these buildings, and they were within arms' reach of weapons that were stationary there or that were, you know, sitting along the floor, along the wall, or lying on the ground or whatever. But I don't recall anyone, except perhaps for the soldier who accompanied me up the stairs, who might have been carrying an AK-47, I don't recall anyone holding a long-barrelled firearm inside the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. During your stay in Sarajevo, did you have an opportunity to visit any sniper emplacements or any locations where snipers were located in the parts of the town, of the city, controlled by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us a more precise location for the emplacements in relation to the part of the city where you were? So in what parts of the city were they?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN HVAAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only went to a Bosnian -- to Bosnian -- or Bosnian government, at that time, Territorial Defence sniper positions, fairly early in the conflict. No. I'll correct that.
